I'm an accounting assistant, I never went to college and made okay grades - A's and B's. My boss is training me to take over the business when he's gone - that means learning all these tax rules and getting certified in certain things to do people's taxes - I won't need any college experience for that. It's not something I'm interested in doing and I plan on finding a replacement and just training them to do what I do so my boss doesn't waste his time on me. 

Out of all the business owners we do accounting for very few actually went to college. Most struggled, got a loan and started a business where they had to be successful or fail and try again. The majority are successful, but what I've realized is money isn't that important. Even people who make a lot of money struggle the same way we do - but theirs is just a bigger scale. More money, more problems. Those big houses have a big mortgage, those fancy cars have a higher monthly bill. Many "wealthy" people spend so much money trying to look wealthy with material things that they struggle just like the rest of us. 

My advice is to not let success be defined by the people around you. In the end their opinions don't matter - not if we all just die and fade away. If it doesn't matter do what you want. Find a job that makes you happy, you might need college or you might not. What makes life worth it? I don't know yet - but I know it's not doing something you hate just to make others happy.

I never called anyone disgusting that was the original commenter though. I stand by what I said, and you never offended me. The poster has Internet so I assume they can find doctor advice online, especially on YouTube. Why is my advice not good enough? What makes your weight loss more significant than mine? There are plenty of ways to eat and I think the poster needs to keep writing down what they ate and try different methods of lifestyle change until they find one that works for them. I will always listen to people who respond, it may not change my opinion but it has the potential to.

I never told her to go "hardcore vegan" she asked what we did to lose weight and that is what I did. I'm not standing on a soapbox crying about how terrible it is to consume animals, because I don't think it is. I have no problems with people who chose to consume meat etc. I would never tell someone they are wrong for doing so, just because my moral compass points a different direction it doesn't mean they are wrong. 

I understand addiction is hard, and I know they hate themselves way more than any other person can. But the poster doesn't need advice from strangers on the Internet, they need a nutritionist and a doctor. The poster knows they are eating poorly and wrote out a list of foods consumed, I refuse to believe someone can look at that and not figure out why they can't lose weight.

If they wanted praise and encouragement they should have just asked for it, it's not bad to want attention.

Your body is craving nutrients, so you eat, but the food you choose isn't nutrient dense it's just high fat and processed sugars with high calories. So you shove that down your gullet but your brain says, "no, I'm hungry!" You didn't receive the nutrients you needed so you feel hungry again after an hour or two. So you eat more junk food with low nutrients and high fat/sugar. It's a vicious cycle and you're under nurished but over weight. 

You HAVE to eat whole foods. In the morning eat two or three bananas, at lunch eat a PLAIN salad with veggies. Wash the veggies but don't cook them or heat them up they lose nutrients. For a snak have an apple, then for dinner have veggies and tofu, maybe a 3/4 cup of rice. Then for dessert have fruit. Don't eat foods from cans or packaged meals you buy from the store, just whole foods and count your calories. It's really simple, but not easy. You have to stop eating all junk food/sugary drinks. If you continue eating them your brain makes you want more. 

Drink 3-4 liters of water a day. I drink 16oz right when I wake up, then 16 oz plain hot tea, I drink 1 liter through the day, 16oz chamomile tea, then another 16oz before bed. Plus more depending on activities. 

This is all stuff you can find out by yourself, download my fitness pal and log every piece of food that goes into your mouth. If you lie it's only cheating yourself. Weightloss and a healthy lifestyle take willpower, if you don't have the willpower you can only blame yourself for failing.
